person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: critique
span.quote: A consideration of the structure of the sentence and of other motor sequences will show, I believe , that such interpretations of temporal organizalion are untenable and that there are , behind the overtly ex pressed sequences, a multiplicity of integrative processes which can only be inferred from the final results of their activity.

span.label: serial order in behavior
span.quote: This is the essential problem of serial order; the existence of generalized schemata of action which determine the sequence of specific acts, acts which in themselves or in their associations seem to have no temporal valence.

span.label: review
span.quote: I shall consider first some of the questions raised by the structure of language, then turn to other forms of serial action for indications of the nature of the nervous mechanisms in,olved.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: serial behavior is produced by a hierarchical central plan (nested orderings of movements, words, sentences), not by associative chains in which each act merely triggers the next
span.quote: There is a series of hierarchies of organization

span.label: the paper formulates the problem but offers no worked-out physiological solution
span.note: what this limits: the paper as a source of mechanism: A CLEARER FORMULATION OF THE PHYSIOLOGICAL PROBLEMS WHICH THEY RAISE SHOULD BE OF VALUE, EVEN THOUGH A SOLUTION OF THE PROBLEMS IS NOT YET IN SIGHT
span.quote: A clearer formulation of the physiological problems which they raise should be of value, even though a solution of the problems is not yet in sight.

span.label: The author states he has no answer to the central question of how particular acts are selected during scanning.
span.note: what this limits: the central question the paper poses: THE REAL PROBLEM ... IS THE NATURE OF THE SELECTIVE MECHANISM BY WHICH THE PARTICULAR ACTS ARE PICKED OUT IN THIS SCANNING PROCESS, AND TO THIS PROBLEM I HAVE NO ANSWER
span.quote: The real problem, however, is the nature of the se lective mechanism by which the particular acts are picked out in this scanning process, and to this problem I have no answer.

span.label: No hypothesis about the selective mechanism of grammatical form proved consistent with any large set of sentence structures.
span.note: what this limits: any account of grammatical form: I HAVE TRIED A NUMBER OF ASSUMPTIONS CONCERNING THE SELECTIVE MECHANISM OF GRAMMATICAL FORM ... BUT I HAVE NEVER BEEN ABLE TO MAKE AN HYPOTHESIS WHICH [held across sentences]
span.quote: I have tried a number of assumptions concerning the selective mechanism of gram matical form ( spatial relations , the relative intensity or prominence of dillerent words in the idea, and so on) but I have never been able to make an hypothesis which was consistent with any large number of sentence structures.

span.label: No explicit explanation of temporal structure is yet available.
span.note: what this limits: the explanatory status of the whole treatment: WE ARE STILL VERY FAR FROM BEING ABLE TO FORM AN EXPLICIT EXPLANATION OF TEMPORAL STRUCTURE
span.quote: However , we are still very far from being able to form an explicit explanation of temporal structure.

span.label: using the hierarchical structure of language (syntax and grammar) as evidence and model for how the brain organizes serial behavior, against associative-chain theories
span.quote: syntax is not inherent in the words employed or in the idea to be expressed

span.label: contradicts → the associative-chain / chain-reflex theory of serial behavior
span.quote: From such considerations it seems to follow that syntax is not inherent in the words employed or in the idea to be expressed.

span.label: contradicts → the peripheral (motor) chain theories of language of Watson and Washburn, and the attempts by Thorsen and Max to confirm them
span.quote: Attempts to confirm these peripheral theories by mechanical (Thorsen, 23) or electrical ( }.[ax, 19) recording of muscular tensions have given no valid evidence in support of them.

span.label: builds-on → Dr. McCulloch's account of the individual neuron's transmission of excitation as the basic principle of nervous organization
span.quote: I agree thoroughly with Dr. McCulloch that the transmjssion of excitation by the individual neuron is the basic principle of nervous organization.

span.label: Lashley argues serial order in behavior CANNOT be explained by associative chain theories (each act triggering the next); order must be centrally, hierarchically organized and imposed as a generalized pattern.
span.quote: syntax is not inherent in the words employed or in the idea to be expressed. It is a generalized pattern imposed upon the specific

span.label: Temporal integration is not exclusive to language — it appears in insect leg coordination, birdsong, gaited horses, and maze-running — pointing to a general hierarchy of central organization.
span.quote: Temporal integration is not found exclusively in language; the coor dination of leg movements in insects, the song of birds, the control of trotting and pacing in a gaited horse, the rat running the maze

span.label: associative chain theory
span.quote: chains of reflexes, in which the performance of each element of the series provides excitation of the next
